title: The two-point question — unwritten apostolic necessities vs equal-authority tradition
source_text: XXIV. Adeoque tota haec quaestio in duobus versatur. Unum est, an Apostoli quaedam necessaria docuerint aut instituerint, quae non sint sufficienter in sacris literis contenta. Alterum, an Apostolorum documenta & instituta aliunde certo & infallibiliter peti & haberi possint, quam ex Scriptura sacra, nempe ex traditione Doctorum Ecclesiae qui Apostolos secuti sunt, cui par obsequium fidei debeatur atque ipsi Scripturae sacrae. Utrumque affirmant Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae: Theologi vero omnes Orthodoxi utrumque negant.
pass_a_gloss: And so this whole question turns on two points. One is whether the Apostles taught or instituted certain necessary things that are not sufficiently contained in the sacred writings. The other is whether the Apostles' documents and institutes can be sought and had with certainty and infallibility from somewhere other than sacred Scripture — namely from the tradition of the Church's doctors who followed the Apostles, to which equal obedience of faith is owed as to sacred Scripture itself. The doctors of the Roman Church affirm both; but all Orthodox theologians deny both.
pass_b_english: The whole question therefore turns on two points.
First: Did the Apostles teach or institute necessary things not sufficiently contained in sacred Scripture?

Second: Can apostolic teaching and institutes be had with certainty and infallibility from somewhere other than Scripture — namely from the tradition of post-apostolic Church doctors, owed equal faith-obedience with Scripture itself?
Rome affirms both. All Orthodox (Reformed) theologians deny both.
